name: Rosy Brown
lede: Rosy Brown is a dusty, pinkish brown, best known today as one of the 140 named colors of the X11 set used on websites.

sections.title: A web color with an old-fashioned name
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary lists RosyBrown as one of the 140 colours in the X11 set used for website design, with the hex code #BC8F8F [1]. The dictionary marks the X11 names with an asterisk in its color index, and files this one among the browns [2].

The wording is plain description. Paterson defines *rosy* as the pinkish red of roses and *rose-wood brown* as a reddish brown [1], so Rosy Brown reads as a brown with some rose in it. The books give no older history for this exact name, and Paterson records it only as a screen-era standard [1]. Nearby entries include [[rosewood]], and in the swatch it sits between [[brown]] and [[pink]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 64 hold this color at 5% of the canvas or more, as photographed [3]. The strongest is Christen Købke's 1832 portrait of Ida Thiele as a child, where it covers about half of the picture [3]. The word *rosy brown* in printed books was most common around 1891, relative to its later use [4].

origin.named_after: X11 web color set (rose plus brown); origin of the name undocumented
origin.first_recorded: X11 set, undated in the books
